outcome_vocabulary_note: ABSENT = no normalized entry matches (covers genuinely absent and dropped in normalization; analysis distinguishes them). EMITTED:<status> = one normalized entry with that status. Statuses were read from source (A1; not runtime-tested): the valid normalized statuses are EMITTED:missing and EMITTED:partial only. A raw no_gap entry is invalid, is dropped by the parser and appears as ABSENT with a diagnostic; the frontend no_gap display state (extracted JD skill with no flagged entry) does not confirm proficiency. The EMITTED:no_gap token in acceptable_outcomes is a retained draft token that cannot occur in normalized output.

assumptions_requiring_review.text: Normalized comparison statuses were read from source (static reading; not runtime-tested): the only valid entry statuses are missing and partial (EMITTED:missing, EMITTED:partial). ABSENT means no matching entry exists in the normalized output. no_gap is not a valid normalized comparison status: the parser drops a raw no_gap entry as an invalid status (leaving ABSENT plus a diagnostic), and the stricter backend and frontend validators would make the whole result unavailable if an invalid entry reached them. The frontend derives a display state no_gap for an extracted JD skill that has no flagged entry; it does not confirm proficiency. The EMITTED:no_gap token in acceptable_outcomes is retained as a draft token only; it cannot occur in normalized output, where the operative outcome is ABSENT.

Course eligibility was read from source (frontend get_recommendation_options; static reading, not runtime-tested): only technical_skills entries are eligible; both missing and partial entries can qualify; entries classified evidence_not_verified (JD quote not found) are skipped and counted as skipped; non-technical entries are neither offered nor counted as skipped; invalid comparison output is unavailable to the frontend eligibility stage. Real-world relevance of recommended courses is untested.

The model, not production code, classifies JD wording into tiers; code only validates the tier names (crucial, good_to_have, optional). Per the comparison prompt as read from source: required, mandatory, must-have, essential or minimum wording -> crucial; preferred, plus, advantage, desirable, nice-to-have or bonus wording -> generally good_to_have; optional when the wording or surrounding section presents the skill as optional or illustrative; ambiguous wording takes the lower tier; a heading is part of the wording. No tier output of the production model has been observed.

Aliases are authored by Claude and matched via the production skill key; alias lists need your review. Production matching uses _skill_key (case-folding, removal of non-alphanumeric characters, trailing-plural removal); it is not semantic or acronym matching, so aliases such as k8s or Amazon Web Services do not match automatically in production (read from source).
